physical.title: blanket
physical.summary: Blanket, cloth (partial); made of cotton. Woven in four and one half wide strips, hand sewn together. White cotton warp and weft. Weft-faced bands in cream, red- and  indigo-dyed cotton aligned across warp strips. Supplementary weft floats in black cotton. Supplementary weft inserts (or tapestry inserts) of elongated lozenge shape and in form of reptile in black cotton. Loose warp thread fringes at both ends.

physical.title: wrapping
physical.summary: Wrapper composed of sixth lengths of hand plain woven narrow strip lengths and a single machine woven length hand sewn together selvedge to selvedge. The narrow strips are composed of dyed indigo warps and wefts and dyed light blue wefts creating light blue cotton warp stripes running the full length of the wrapper. The wrapper consists of a single machine woven bleached white length embroidered  with a repeating geometric pattern in dyed brown cotton which is flanked by three widths of narrow strip woven cotton. The warp ends are lined with printed fabric.

cultural.vision_reason: This is a hand-woven strip-cloth wall hanging with supplementary-weft geometric patterning, a type of narrow-strip weaving associated with Hausa marriage/prestige textiles in Niger; the object and description are consistent with the claimed ethnicity.

physical.title: wall-hanging; marriage equipment
physical.summary:
Wall hanging "Niger". Rectangular piece, composed of nine (9) hand-woven narrow cotton-threads strips hand-sewn together selvedge-to-selvedge. The decoration is organised in transverse bands with continuous weft-faced arrangement. Decorations are done in supplementary weft technique. There are 
- five white background bands with black design in form of two pairs of opposed triangles and bars
- four white background bands with red design in form of two pairs of opposed triangles and bars
- five black bands decorated with groups of four coloured lozenges (green, red, yellow, and white)
- two black bands decorated with the number "1991"
- three plain black bands: two at one end and one at the other end.

The strips end in loose warp threads.

Two abnormalities:
1. Two srips had been sewn the wrong way around, creating discontinuity in the weft-faced band.
2. In one strip a red design had been made instead of a black one, and a black design instead of a red one.
